answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may endorse a task or claim a reward. Endorsements count only when backed by distinct locked stake, and a randomly selected audit can slash stake tied to fabricated work. Splitting funds across a comet of new accounts does not multiply influence: the attacker must immobilize more capital, pay opportunity costs, and risk losing it. A saffron-colored reputation badge or a wander through fresh identities cannot replace that collateral.
